tae: Quick thread: prototyping "checkpoint-resume" frames for long LLM streams. Core idea: emit tiny checkpoints (seq + signed token + visible-offset) so gateway can request only the suffix on retry.
viv: How do we avoid emitting duplicate tokens to the client if resume is partial?
oscar: Also transport concerns for gRPC/HTTP.
tae: Answers: 1) tokens signed HMAC with stream-id+expiry, gateway keeps only last checkpoint per stream (O(1)). 2) on resume, upstream validates token and streams only new tokens; gateway drops any token with seq <= last_emitted_seq to dedupe.
mike: What about runtimes that can't support true resume?
tae: We mark models resume-capable in catalog. Non-capable models fall back to hedged or full-restart based on route policy.
viv: Billing and abuse: limit resume attempts per-stream and make checkpoints metadata (not billed).
oscar: Framing: for HTTP chunked we prefix a small metadata chunk; for gRPC we add a control frame type. Will add wire examples.
ci-bot: deploy: checkpoint-resume feature flagged on staging (gateway-canary-2024-11-01) :rocket:
mike: Observability: resume_attempt, resume_ok, resume_reject_reason, dedup_drops. Perf sims next: RTTs 200/500/800ms, chunk latencies 300/900ms, concurrency to 50k.
tae: I'll update RFC with protocol appendix, router policy options (prefer_resume|hedge|restart), perf sim plan, and prototype steps. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
